# Test txtar format input
# We use a helper script to create the txtar content

# First, create a proper txtar file using the embedded data
cp chart_template.json chart.json
cat chart.json

# Create a txtar file with the cat command
# (scripttest extracts files at the same level, so we need to create it manually)

# For now, verify the basic JSON loading works as a baseline
sc validate chart.json
stdout 'VALID'

# Test info
sc info chart.json
stdout 'States:'
stdout 'Transitions: 3'

# Test states
sc states chart.json
stdout 'Idle'
stdout 'Running'
stdout 'Stopped'

-- chart_template.json --
{
  "root_state": {
    "label": "__root__",
    "type": 2,
    "children": [
      {"label": "Idle", "type": 1, "is_initial": true},
      {"label": "Running", "type": 1},
      {"label": "Stopped", "type": 1}
    ]
  },
  "transitions": [
    {"from": ["Idle"], "to": ["Running"], "event": "START"},
    {"from": ["Running"], "to": ["Stopped"], "event": "STOP"},
    {"from": ["Stopped"], "to": ["Idle"], "event": "RESET"}
  ],
  "events": [
    {"label": "START"},
    {"label": "STOP"},
    {"label": "RESET"}
  ]
}
